title: Graveyard Scene by Tom Lovell
content: This 1947 illustration by Tom Lovell for True Magazine was for an article called "Extra Corpse in the Graveyard." It's a good image to study for color and composition.Color and Value• You could probably paint this with Venetian red, viridian, and white, maybe with a touch of raw umber and yellow ochre.• Note the grouping of tones in the white gravestones and the simplicity of the grassy ground texture.• Tones are also grouped in the dark background trees and in the shadowed foreground grasses.Composition• Except for the walking figure, all the other key elements are cropped intriguingly: the arm, the gravestone with its fragmentary name, and the white gravestone on the right.• This design is not an obvious one, and I would guess that Lovell arrived at this composition after doing a lot of tonal thumbnails in pencil.• Positioning the hand in the extreme foreground also places viewer in the grave and in the path of discovery.-----Books:Tom Lovell-IllustratorThe Art of Tom Lovell: An Invitation to HistoryTom Lovell : Storyteller with a Brush
